deviations.1_World_lastPlanId_and_Plan_shape: ACCEPTED. ids that never repeat need a counter outside the journey (a cancelled plan would otherwise let id 1 recur); Plan {id, target, from, heading, flip, trip: TripPlan} keeps the package's TripPlan whole, which is what makes checkPlanIsPackage a bit-for-bit check; Committed/Arrived carrying {plan, tau0, t0} is what freezes the committed panel.
deviations.2_stale_plan_covers_another_position: ACCEPTED. A plan's d and heading are from where it was made; committing it from elsewhere would fly the wrong trip. Exact position equality is right here: in play the ship cannot move between plan and commit, and in diag any move changes position() by far more than an ulp.
deviations.3_out_of_range_for_zero_distance_and_non: ACCEPTED. No heading exists for a target at the ship's position and planFlipAndBurn requires a > 0; refusing with the existing range code is better than a new reason or a crash in the package's `requires`.
deviations.4_cancel_without_a_plan_is_a_no_op: ACCEPTED. The design says cancel 'clears an uncommitted plan'; with nothing to clear there is nothing to refuse. The design's reason-code row was updated to say so.
deviations.5_echo_draw_record_refused_committed: ACCEPTED (stricter than the design's list). It makes the rule one line per constructor with no wildcard, which is the whole point of Pillar 1 in code.
deviations.6_planned_panel_is_live: ACCEPTED. D-12 says the clock runs while planning, so arrive_year/age_on_arrival/years_left must move; re-sending the section each tick follows the change-set rule literally. Cost is ~1 KB per tick while a plan is open; acceptable at the bridge's rate, worth a glance when M2.6a wires the panel.
deviations.7_exhaustiveness_enforced_by_test: ACCEPTED with a note. ailang check does not reject a non-exhaustive match (DX report filed), so the design's 'fails to compile' is unavailable. The test enumerates today's eight constructors; a ninth added without an arm would be a runtime match error in refuseWhileCommitted rather than an accepted intent, so the failure mode is fail-safe (the sim stops, it never accepts). The design text should be amended (see documentation deduction).
deviations.8_underscore_arm_workaround_ailang_1473: ACCEPTED. `_ => j` in cancelPlan (core.ail:213) is semantically identical to `other => other`; the comment cites the issue so it can be reverted when fixed.
deviations.9_updated_checkTickRefusals_checkRefused: ACCEPTED. The expected refusal lists changed because cancel is now a no-op and plan/commit are real; checkRefusedProceeds now also asserts the journey section nets to no change after plan+commit(moving)+cancel in one tick, which is a stronger test than before.

verdict: PASS 95/100. All six M2.3a acceptance commands re-run green in a fresh worktree on v0.50.0 with relativity 0.4.0; make test exits 0 (67 AILANG tests, bridge 0 failures, three parity targets, strict protocolVm/worldVm/planVm VM == interpreter). The alpha Cen 0.99c panel the sim emits is bit-equal to my independent python from the package formulas (ship 0.6226958707592057 yr, Earth 4.414143655383168 yr, boost 1.7979782022600483 min, total 6.1276428633128384e17 J = 6.817922175341585 kg, drag 23.25982143207345 N, T_fwd 38.44085554458952 K) and reproduces HB-35/40/49/53/62. d is float64 scalars, 1-beta is the rapidity form, every readout is a package output. The commit rule lives in the sim with one arm per constructor and no wildcard; by code audit and by a wire session, nothing leads from Committed back to Planned or Idle and every intent kind is refused `committed`. All nine declared deviations are accepted. Non-blocking: two low-severity test gaps (plan distance from a moved ship, the moving-guard boundary), two doc sentences in section M2.3 to amend, and the changelog at landing.
